archetype.name: Fringe Contender (all offense)
archetype.definition: A top-six offense chained to a bottom-two defense, good enough to stay in a soft NFC East race but too leaky to control games, so the record depends on who has the ball last.

report.headline: Last year's team again: Prescott's offense carries it, the defense gives it back
report.take:
Dallas is running last season back almost exactly. In 2025 the offense ranked 5th in EPA and the defense ranked 32nd; this year the offense is 6th (0.112 EPA a play) and the defense 31st (0.101 allowed). Dak Prescott has started all ten games, CeeDee Lamb has drawn 121 targets with George Pickens at 80 behind him, and the attack works both ways: 6th in pass EPA, and the run game is a genuine plus behind a line that ranks 8th in run success. The result is a team that scores 28.6 a game and allows 28.2. That is not a bad team. It is a coin flip that keeps landing in shootouts.

The 4-6 record undersells that coin flip, but only a little. A +4 point differential implies 5.5 wins, so Dallas is about a win and a half short (-1.45 wins over expected), mostly because it has gone 1-for-3 in the one-score games that matter: a three-point loss to Baltimore, a three-point loss to Arizona, a six-point loss to San Francisco, all with 30 or more points on the board. Turnovers aren't to blame for much. The margin is close to even at -3. The real problem is the defense. Opponents convert 48.3% on third down, worst in the league, and score touchdowns on 67.6% of red-zone trips. Offenses also lean on the run against Dallas more than almost anyone, since its rush EPA allowed ranks dead last. When a defense can't get off the field, every close game turns into whoever has the ball last.

Two things the averages smooth over. First, the offense's floor shows up against real defenses. Its only two duds, 16 points against Tampa Bay and 13 at Green Bay, came against defenses now ranked 2nd and 7th, and both featured multiple giveaways. Second, the Book has been burned by this team. Dallas covers only 37.5% of the time and lost outright both times it was favored by a touchdown or more (Tampa Bay at -9.5, Arizona at -7). This offense wins shootouts against bad defenses; it does not reliably blow anyone out.

Where it goes depends on the next two weeks. Tennessee (1-8) and Philadelphia (2-7) come to Dallas back to back. After that the schedule runs through Seattle, the Rams and Jacksonville, defenses ranked 5th, 3rd and 4th, which is exactly the kind of unit that has stalled this offense. With the Giants leading the division at 5-3-1 and two division games left at the end, the path to January is to bank both home games now and split the rest. That has to happen with guard Tyler Booker and corner DaRon Bland both out from last week's loss to the 49ers.

strengths.title: A balanced, top-five offense
strengths.body: Dallas ranks 5th in offensive EPA and success rate. It is equally efficient through the air and on the ground, which is rare for an offense this pass-centric. The cause is stable: the same quarterback every week, a clear target pecking order with Lamb then Pickens, and a run game that keeps the offense on schedule rather than piling up empty volume. History backs it up, since this unit was top five last year too. It should hold, with the caveat that its worst games came against elite defenses.

strengths.title: Line keeps Prescott clean
strengths.body: A 3.8% sack rate ranks 5th, and the line also ranks 8th in run success. Time to throw is middling, so this is protection holding up, not a quarterback throwing hot. It is the foundation of the offense's consistency. It is also the strength most exposed right now, with starting guard Tyler Booker (94% of snaps) out until December.

strengths.title: Record trails the differential
strengths.body: The point differential says 5.5 wins, not four. The gap comes from a poor record in one-score games, not from a turnover-fuelled mirage. That makes the 4-6 slightly better than it looks, though a team whose defense forces this many coin flips will keep losing some of them.

concerns.title: A defense that never gets off the field
concerns.body: Dallas is last in defensive EPA by play-by-play and last in third-down defense, so drives against it rarely end early. This is not a one-year blip: the 2025 defense also ranked 32nd. A unit that has been bottom-of-the-league for two straight seasons is structural, and it is why even 40 points wasn't enough against San Francisco.

concerns.title: Run defense invites ball control
concerns.body: Opponents pass four points less often than normal against Dallas, among the strongest run funnels in the league. They are right to: the rush EPA allowed ranks last and the explosive-run rate allowed ranks 27th. Tampa Bay ran for 241 yards in a win at Dallas. Any opponent with a functional run game can shorten the game and keep this offense on the sideline.

concerns.title: Secondary thinning where it already bleeds
concerns.body: Opposing WR1s score more over their norm against Dallas than against any other defense. The short passing game is also a problem, ranking 29th in EPA allowed. Now DaRon Bland, an 89%-snap corner, is out with a high-ankle sprain, along with safety P.J. Locke. The coverage problem is real and is about to get thinner.

trend.note: The offense slumped against Tampa Bay and Green Bay in October, then rebounded to 27 or more in each of the last four games. Results still alternated win-loss, because the defense gave up 33 and 46 in the two losses.

nextGame.headline: Lamb against the league's leakiest big-play defense, at home
nextGame.body:
Tennessee is 1-8 and its offense ranks 27th in EPA and 31st in yards per game. That is the kind of attack even this Dallas defense can survive. The Titans' defense has one real weapon: a pressure rate that ranks 4th. Behind it, the coverage is a sieve. It allows explosive passes more often than anyone and ranks 31st in WR1 production over the norm, which points straight at Lamb's 121 targets. It tackles well and is respectable against the run, so the cleanest path for Dallas is through the air. The Book makes Dallas an 8.5-point favorite with a 54.5 total. That is a big number for a team that covers 37.5% of the time and has already lost outright as a 9.5- and 7-point favorite.

Availability cuts both ways. Dallas is without guard Tyler Booker, which matters against that Titans rush, plus corner DaRon Bland, linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku, tight end Jake Ferguson and safety P.J. Locke; backup back Tyler Goodson is on IR. Tennessee is missing more of its core. Linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. (100% of snaps) and Cody Barton are both out, guard Peter Skoronski is on IR, receiver Carnell Tate is listed out though his coach is hopeful, Wan'Dale Robinson is questionable, safety Tony Adams is in the concussion protocol, and their punter is on IR.

waysToWin.title: Feed Lamb against a broken secondary
waysToWin.body: Tennessee gives up explosive passes more often than any defense and ranks 26th in pass EPA allowed. Its WR1s run well above their norms, nearly a mirror of Dallas's own problem. With Hill and Barton out at linebacker, the middle of the field should open further. Dallas's 6th-ranked passing game should score at will if Prescott has time.

waysToWin.title: Pin the ears back on Ward
waysToWin.body: Tennessee's line allows pressure at the 3rd-highest rate and has lost guard Skoronski (97% of snaps) to IR. Dallas pressures at a top-twelve rate and just had five sacks against San Francisco. Pressure is the one way this defense reliably ends drives, and this matchup gives it plenty of chances.

waysToWin.title: Force Tennessee to keep pace
waysToWin.body: The Titans rank last in time of possession and 27th in offensive EPA. They are not built to trade touchdowns. An early two-score lead takes them out of the ball-control plan that beats Dallas.

waysToLose.title: Pressure without Booker, then giveaways
waysToLose.body: Tennessee's pass rush ranks 4th in pressure rate, and Dallas is missing a 94%-snap starting guard. The Tampa Bay loss is the template: a big favorite turning it over three times against a strong defensive front. Turnovers are the one thing that sinks this offense.

waysToLose.title: Titans run it down Dallas's throat
waysToLose.body: Dallas's run defense ranks last in EPA allowed, and Tennessee averages a respectable 4.06 yards a carry. Tennessee already prefers the run. If it sustains drives on the ground and Dallas keeps failing on third down, the game stays close into the fourth quarter, where Dallas has struggled.

waysToLose.title: Flags hand back field position
waysToLose.body: Dallas ranks 26th in penalties per game and was flagged for 153 yards even in the win at Indianapolis. Against a team that can't drive the field, penalties are how a 1-8 opponent gets short fields and stays in the game.

nextGame.watch: Booker's replacement against Tennessee's interior rush on early downs: if Prescott is clean, Lamb feasts; if he isn't, this becomes the Tampa Bay game again.

restOfSeason.body:
The offense is the sustainable part. It was top five last year with the same quarterback and is top six now, so expect points in bunches against Tennessee, Philadelphia and Washington. Expect less against the three elite defenses in the middle of the run: Seattle, the Rams and Jacksonville, the profile that produced this team's 13- and 16-point games. The defense is also likely to stay bad, since it has been bottom-two for two seasons. Bland's return later in the month helps the pass coverage but does nothing for the run defense or third downs.

Some positive regression in close games is fair to expect, because the differential runs ahead of the record. But this defense keeps producing coin flips, and it won't win most of them. The likely shape is wins over the two bad NFC East teams and Tennessee, losses in some of the tough three, and a Week 17 home game against the Giants that decides whether Dallas is chasing the division or a wild card.
swingFactors: Pass protection without Booker against Seattle, the Rams and Jacksonville
The Week 17 home game with the Giants

confidence.note: Ten games that mirror the 2025 profile, but a pile of fresh injuries.
